title: Does fitting a webcam-signal generator to one person fool a detector that has seen that person?
lede: does fitting to one person help? Copying a person's own earlier windows is caught at AUROC 0.59 to 0.65 on their later windows; copying other people is 0.58 to 0.91, and 0.93 to 0.97 once the detector knows the person; a fitted parametric generator is caught at 1.000 either way.
summary: Each of 46 DUX webcam-signal people (12 to 54 ten-second windows) is split in time: generators see the first half only, a boosted-tree detector separates the second half from generated windows (6 seeds). Drawing 50-frame blocks from the person's own earlier windows gives AUROC 0.654 (join-matched 0.565, whole-window replay 0.593); drawing them from other people gives 0.913 (0.833, 0.582), rising to 0.971 (0.959, 0.926) when the detector is also given the person's mean level and spread. A fitted parametric generator (window levels, AR(1), channel correlation, holds) is caught at 1.000 whether fitted on one person or on everyone. So person-specific style is most of what separates copies from people; a fitted generator is still far from it. Stylised: one form-filling context; copies are ceilings, not generators.
